messages:
deploy-bot: [automated] publish failed for py-ts-sdk 1.8.0 - checksum_mismatch on dist/redwood_py_ts-1.8.0-py3-none-any.whl
maya: saw this in the release monitor. holding the change window. can someone check the CI signing + upload?
chris: on it. was this from the canary publish pipeline or ad-hoc?
noah: came from ci/publish/canary job. twine returned 200 but post-publish integrity check failed. log excerpt below:
```
verify-wheel: sha256 expected=9f3b2a... got=9f3b2b...
uploader: ci-agent-17
artifact-size: 2.4MB
```
jen: quick sanity check - I pulled the wheel and ran `gpg --verify` locally, sig OK. suggests registry object mismatch rather than signing key compromise.
sam: if registry object is corrupted we should yank 1.8.0 ASAP and pin docs to 1.7.4. downstream infra should keep stable installs.
release-oncall: agreed. do we have a short rollback play?
chris: PyPI supports yanking. I can yank 1.8.0 now and block the canary tag in our release controller. will also open a GH issue to track republish.
noah: before yank, can we re-run the verify-only job to fetch the uploaded artifact and validate? `ci/verify-artifact` can re-fetch from registry and compare shas. if it succeeds maybe a transient read got fixed.
maya: prefer Yank first to avoid any accidental installs, then re-verify + re-upload if appropriate.
chris: yanked 1.8.0 on pypi, blocked canary move, created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-ts-sdk/issues/1429 for republish.
deploy-bot: [automated] ticket created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-ts-sdk/pull/1429
noah: kicking off `ci/verify-artifact` #863 to validate what landed. if verify fails we rebuild and publish 1.8.1+ci.863 to avoid caching reuse.
jen: security note: since local gpg checks passed, prioritize storage integrity checks. I ran quick `sha256sum` locally on the artifact we built and it matches the CI expected digest.
sam: ops checklist once we have a good artifact: 1) run verify job 2) publish new artifact 3) un-yank 4) move canary tag 5) update docs + changelog 6) announce in release-channels.
infra-oncall: oncall here. I'll tail S3 upload logs / registry replication in the next 15m and report findings.
maya: I'll update the public changelog entry with a short note: "1.8.0 yanked pending integrity verification; using 1.7.4 while we republish." also notify integrators in #general.
noah: verify job started. if it fails I'll trigger a rebuild pipeline with incremental build metadata bump: 1.8.1+ci.863 to ensure new artifact object key.
chris: once republished, we'll also rotate the canary tag only after CI verification passes and we do a smoke test against the quickstart.
jen: add a line in the internal deprecation/pin doc so infra teams know which Dockerfiles/lockfiles to pin during the change window.
sam: good. if verify fails, escalate to infra for deeper S3/registry investigation.
infra-oncall: pulled replication logs - one object PUT had a 503 retry around the time of upload. digging into backend retries now.
maya: thanks. keeping this thread canonical for the yank + republish decision. will follow up here with final artifact sha and release note when complete. :thumbsup:
